headline: Tehran 'deliberately prolonged talks with the US to try to weaken Donald Trump politically ahead of November's US midterm
dek: Iran deliberately prolonging US talks to weaken Trump politically ahead of Nov 3 midterms; Tehran preparing for renewed attacks, not a deal; 'determined not to give Trump a political victory'; little chance of breakthrough before elections.
sources: Reuters (Parisa Hafezi, ); three senior Iranian officials + one Iranian insider (all anonymous); named analyst Saeed Leylaz
fault_line: Is Tehran really weaponizing the US election clock — or is Washington's blockade the actual reason nothing moves?

sections.what_happened: Iran deliberately prolonging US talks to weaken Trump politically ahead of Nov 3 midterms; Tehran preparing for renewed attacks, not a deal; 'determined not to give Trump a political victory'; little chance of breakthrough before elections.
sections.what_verified: Economic Times, NDTV Profit, apa.az, BOE Report, WYSL all relay the Reuters exclusive verbatim; consistent with Ghalibaf's 'nothing new to offer' (arabtimesonline Oct 20) and Araghchi's demand that Islamabad MOU be honored first (Gulf News Oct 21).
sections.what_disputed: Al Araby Al Jadeed report (Oct 20) claims Iran gave 'preliminary agreement in principle' to Qatar-Pakistan proposal — directly contradicted by these officials; Qatar FM (via Fox News per MEF digest) says talks continue; officials are anonymous so motive claims are attributed, not independently verifiable.
sections.why_matters: Tehran's election clock: Iran refuses to hand Trump a pre-midterms win — the Hormuz lever works until November 3. Side-of-truth framing: Tehran's position stated as its strategy, not a Western accusation.
sections.context: Background: Iran diplomacy — NEW: Reuters exclusive (Oct 20, Parisa Hafezi): Tehran 'deliberately prolonged talks with the US to try to weaken Donald Trump politically ahead of November's US midterm elections'; officials say Iran is 'preparing for renewed Israeli and US attacks, not for a deal with America'; Tehran analyst Saeed Leylaz: 'Iran is influencing the US election without taking any unlawful action'; war has driven Trump's approval to record low as gasoline prices punish Republicans ahead of Nov 3

totw_analysis: Our read: Tehran's election clock: Iran refuses to hand Trump a pre-midterms win — the Hormuz lever works until November 3. Side-of-truth framing: Tehran's position stated as its strategy, not a Western accusation. The fault line our audience is arguing over: Is Tehran really weaponizing the US election clock — or is Washington's blockade the actual reason nothing moves?
